_comment: Registry for Lightspeed Retail X-Series. Holds the API connection config, the outlet name that is baked into three CSV column headers, the category vocabulary, and the rate-limit tuning. It does NOT duplicate the LS upload column mapping — that stays in the ls-upload-instructions skill, which is the single source for column ORDER and name construction. Consumed by scripts/lightspeed_client.py, scripts/lightspeed_pull.py and (from Phase 4) .claude/agents/lightspeed-actions-agent.md. Titan is on X-Series, confirmed live 2026-09-10 against flooru.retail.lightspeed.app. NOT R-Series.
_maintenance: api_version is pinned deliberately. Lightspeed is deprecating semantic API versions (2.0) in favour of date-based versioning (e.g. 2026-01); 2.0 receives no new features. When migrating, change it here and re-run scripts/lightspeed_pull.py --probe, then --compare-export against the two committed LS workbooks, before any write runs. domain_prefix and the personal token come from .env — see .env.example. VERIFIED LIVE 2026-09-10: the pagination envelope, the version cursor and the rate-limit numbers below are measured, not assumed. api_shape records what a product actually looks like — it differs from the CSV import/export columns in three ways that matter, all noted there.

api._comment: Base URL is per-retailer. domain_prefix is the <prefix> in <prefix>.retail.lightspeed.app and comes from LIGHTSPEED_DOMAIN_PREFIX; it is not a secret but is account-identifying, so it is not hardcoded here.
api._api_version_note: Pinned. See _maintenance — 2.0 is deprecated in favour of date-based versioning.

auth._token_note: A personal token grants the SAME DATA ACCESS AS AN ADMIN USER and is NOT scopable — there is no read-only variant. Generate it at Setup > Personal tokens > Generate personal token, always WITH an expiry. It lives in .env only. Cloud env vars are not a secrets store (see .env.example). The read-only guarantee on the pull side is structural, not permission-based: scripts/lightspeed_pull.py has no write code path.
auth._scoped_alternative: A genuinely scoped credential requires building an OAuth Add-on with products:read / products:write. Judged not worth it for a single-retailer internal tool; revisit if this ever runs for anyone but Titan.

pagination._comment: Cursor pagination on the `version` attribute carried by every collection resource. Pass the last seen version as `after`; page until fewer than page_size records come back.
pagination._verified: Confirmed live 2026-09-10. Response is {"data": [...], "version": {"min": N, "max": N}}; `version.max` is the next `after`, and every record carries its own `version`. 15 pages of 1000 walked the catalogue with the cursor advancing monotonically and no repeats.

api._no_bulk_endpoint: There is no bulk product create/update endpoint — bulk import is UI/CSV only. Every product is one HTTP call. This is why the sync runs as a script rather than a Make scenario metered per operation.
api._no_supplier_filter: The products endpoint has no server-side supplier filter. The pull walks the whole catalogue once, caches it, and filters locally.

_versions._comment: Version sprawl is real and per-operation. Confirmed against the API reference 2026-09-10. Do not assume one version covers everything.
_versions.create_product: 2.0  POST /api/2.0/products — creates a product or a whole variant family.
_versions.update_product: 2.1  PUT /api/2.1/products/{id} — `common` + `details` sections. The 2.1 update CANNOT create variants.
_versions.read_family: 3.0  GET /api/3.0/products/{id} — returns the family with a `variants` array.
_versions.current_dated: The reference now publishes as date-versioned `2026-07`, served at /api/2026-07. 2.0/2.1/3.0 are the legacy semantic versions. Migrate deliberately; re-verify with --probe and --compare-export first.
_versions.add_variant_to_family: 2.1  POST /api/2.1/products/ — adds a variant to an EXISTING family. Distinct from the 2.0 POST that creates a family, and from the 2.1 PUT that updates one and explicitly cannot create variants.

rate_limits._comment: Two independent limiters. The primary is a leaky bucket sized by the retailer's register count. The secondary is a BURST limiter on 1-second fixed windows, which means a minimum interval between requests matters more than average throughput. Both surface via headers when they block.
rate_limits.backoff: honour Retry-After when present; otherwise exponential from min_interval_ms

_observed.note: A full walk at page_size 1000 with min_interval_ms 250 never tripped either limiter. 1000 is accepted and returns full pages. There is headroom, but nothing downstream needs a faster read — the walk is cached per day.

rate_limits._observed_note: Populate from the first live pull: the actual bucket size, the burst window allowance, and whether min_interval_ms of 250 ever trips the burst limiter.
rate_limits._abort_policy: On repeated 429 or any 5xx, STOP THE BATCH, log, report — the house rule for actions agents. Resume is re-running the command: every completed action is already in the day's actions-log.json and is skipped.

outlet._comment: Read live from GET /api/2.0/outlets 2026-09-10. There is exactly one outlet, and it is NOT named 'Titan Flooring' — this file previously said it was, inferred from the LS upload CSV column suffixes.
outlet.name: Mississauga Outlet
outlet._display_prices_note: Authoritative confirmation of the tax-exclusive model that api_shape.prices established empirically.
outlet._csv_column_mismatch: WORTH CHECKING. The LS upload CSV built by ls-upload-instructions uses the column headers outlet_tax_Titan Flooring, inventory_Titan Flooring, reorder_point_Titan Flooring and restock_level_Titan Flooring. The skill states the suffix must match the outlet name exactly, and the outlet is named 'Mississauga Outlet'. Those four columns have therefore most likely been ignored on every CSV import to date. Little practical harm — products fall back to the outlet default tax, and the inventory columns are documented as left blank anyway — but the headers are wrong and the API path should use the id above rather than any name.

product_categories._comment: LS requires a LEAF category — an intermediate node is rejected with 'A product can only be assigned to a leaf category'. 42 Grandeur rows were rejected on this in July 2026. Format is all caps, space-slash-space separated.
product_categories._vinyl_note: The vinyl subcategory is decided by the product's CORE (SPC or WPC), never by its format (LVP or LVT).
product_categories._accessories_note: Accessories (transitions, mouldings, stair treads/risers, underlay, glue) use the standalone ACCESSORIES category — not nested under FLOORING.
product_categories._unmapped_policy: A product whose category does not resolve to one of `leaves` is BLOCKED, never guessed.
product_categories._csv_vs_api: The `leaves` list below is the CSV-IMPORTER form. The API returns leaf names alone — see api_shape.category. Keep both straight: a write path built on the API cannot reuse this list unchanged.

api_write_category_ids._comment: REFERENCE ONLY — no code reads this block. Salvaged 2026-09-23 from funny-rubin-4puvl1 (d75ff7b, 2026-09-11). It records that LAMINATE, TILE and VINYL each have TWO live product_type ids, a pre-existing duplicate in the account. Since 70f142f (salvaged the same day), scripts/lightspeed_push.py Lookups.resolve() REFUSES a duplicated name rather than picking one, so a laminate/tile/vinyl create stops until either the duplicate is merged in the Lightspeed UI or the resolver is taught to read a pin from here. That is Albert's call; the ids below are the evidence for it.
api_write_category_ids._ambiguous_names_pinned_here: ENGINEERED HARDWOOD, SOLID HARDWOOD, SPC, WPC and ACCESSORIES each have exactly one live id and need no pin — Lookups.resolve() finds them safely by name alone. LAMINATE, TILE and VINYL do NOT: each has TWO distinct live ids (487 vs 383 products on LAMINATE alone, confirmed 2026-09-11), a genuine pre-existing duplicate-category defect in the live account, not something this pipeline may unify. Lookups.resolve() would silently pick whichever the API lists first — non-deterministic and never verified. Any such name MUST be pinned here before a create write path may use it; an unpinned ambiguous name should block, never guess.
api_write_category_ids._tile_pin_rationale: Albert, 2026-09-23 (PL-372): "use the TILE that is nested in FLOORING Parent". Live: 7bce055e has category_path FLOORING / TILE; 0a6f6e36-8b89-11eb-f3d6-58434e81cb4c is a root-level TILE (older JL/Sidco/Kisense/Northway products sit there). Enforced in code, not read from here: Lookups.resolve() indexes nested types by full path, so an LS CSV category of FLOORING / TILE resolves to 7bce055e and bare TILE still refuses. Same mechanism resolves FLOORING / LAMINATE to 08f5e5d9, agreeing with the pin above. Existing products were NOT re-filed.
api_write_category_ids._laminate_pin_rationale: Two ids exist (02dcd191-ae89-11e8-ed44-9bffc29c1504: 487 products, most-recent update 2026-09-03; 08f5e5d9-16e1-4fa0-8b64-78d71bbe55c5: 383 products, most-recent update 2026-09-10 on LAM-FAWK-0035). Pinned to the second because it is the id this same pipeline's own recent creates already use — not because it is provably 'more correct'. Flagged for Albert; the live duplicate itself is unresolved infra debt.

write_rules._comment: The invariants any write path must respect. Full detail and the name-construction rules live in the ls-upload-instructions skill.
write_rules.id_semantics: A populated `id` is an UPDATE; a blank `id` is a CREATE. A blank id on a row that already exists in Lightspeed creates a DUPLICATE instead of updating. Grandeur 2026-09-03: a colour-only backfill gave 7 UUIDs to 16 rows and LS rejected 9 with 'handle already exists for your retailer, sku already exists for your retailer'.
write_rules.identified_by: NAME, not handle. Two products may not share a name.
write_rules.handle_is_the_variant_key: Rows sharing a handle become variants of one parent. Letters and numbers only.
write_rules.sku_no_commas: LS rejects commas in a SKU.
never: write a row whose match is ambiguous or duplicate
write_rules._variants_unverified: HALF SETTLED 2026-09-21, by a real create rather than the planned spike. SETTLED: a STANDALONE product. POST /api/2.0/products with sku, prices and outlet_taxes at the TOP level and NO `variants` key created LVP-FAWK-0084 (db9e9a99-afb5-4173-8193-6ea68798d80a) correctly — verified by a full re-pull: 14,836 products, exactly one row for the sku, has_variants false, variant_options [], no duplicate. STILL UNVERIFIED: a MULTI-MEMBER family. The API creates one as a single POST carrying a `variants` array plus `variant_definitions`, and adding a variant to an EXISTING family is a different call, so row-by-row POST still will not reproduce CSV-importer behaviour. No family of more than one has been created through this path. Do not assume that shape until a create proves it — the standalone case was assumed from the read model too, and was wrong twice running (api_shape.variants._family_id, and .create._variants_array_is_not_for_simple_products).

make_scenarios._comment: What Make does and does not do for Lightspeed, recorded so it is not re-litigated.

intake_trigger.name: Price Lists
intake_trigger.role: Outlook attachment -> OneDrive -> anonymous share link -> Notion Price Lists row -> webhook {notionID}. UNCHANGED by this pipeline; it stays in Make.

superseded_draft.name: DRAFT - Lightspeed Product Upsert (from LS upload CSV)
superseded_draft.why_superseded: Row-by-row vend:MakeAPICall POST with no connection, no error handling, no UUID capture. Make's `vend` app has no Update a Product module, so updates would be hand-written API JSON inside Make anyway — the API path minus version control, tests and dry-run. Also meters per row against a 40,000 ops/month Core plan already carrying ~25 scenarios.

make_scenarios._blueprint_editing_warning: Do NOT edit large Make blueprints through scenarios_update. Stripping `metadata` to fit the token limit FAILS SILENTLY: the runtime needs metadata.expect, and without it the module executes, consumes an operation, makes a real round-trip, drops the payload, writes nothing, and returns SUCCESS. Edit in the Make UI. See methods/pricelist-extraction.md.

api_shape._comment: What a product actually looks like on the API, measured over all 14,525 products 2026-09-10. Recorded because the API and the CSV import/export are DIFFERENT vocabularies for the same catalogue — the ls-upload-instructions skill describes the CSV, and anything talking to the API needs the mapping below.

join_key._why: The only safe join. Unique and always present: 0 blanks and 0 duplicates across 14,525 products. This is also what --compare-export proved, reconciling 267/267 Grandeur and 311/311 Canadian Standard UUIDs against the hand-made exports.

identity.id: uuid, assigned by LS on create
identity.handle: variant grouping key, shared across a family

supplier._do_not_join_on_this: 116 distinct supplier names live in LS against 24 Airtable supplier choices, and several real suppliers are split across more than one LS record: OLYMPIA (292) beside Olympia Tile (2926), LEE (2) beside Lee Flooring (84), UMB beside Umbrellar, MARMOCA beside MARMOCA TILE, CIF Distributors beside CIF LTD. Casing is inconsistent too. Supplier is a reporting field; join on sku.
supplier._third_namespace: Notion Company is ALL CAPS, Airtable Supplier is mixed case, and LS is its own thing again — mostly upper but not always. Three namespaces, none aligned. Airtable <-> Notion is in airtable-destinations.json supplier_aliases; LS is deliberately not mapped, because it does not need to be once the join is on sku.

_record_rulings_2026_09_21._comment: Albert's rulings on the duplicate/near-duplicate supplier records surfaced 2026-09-21 while tracing how the create path resolves a supplier by name. Recorded so none of these gets 'tidied' the wrong way later. The merges and deletions are done by hand in the Lightspeed UI — this pipeline has no supplier merge, rename or delete capability, deliberately.
_record_rulings_2026_09_21.OLYMPIA + OLYMPIA TILE: MERGE into 'OLYMPIA TILE', which is also the canonical name in Airtable. Was OLYMPIA (292 products) beside OLYMPIA TILE (2,926).
_record_rulings_2026_09_21.TOSCA/VICEROY: DELETE. 0 products against it; TOSCA (447) is the real record.
_record_rulings_2026_09_21.LEE + Lee Flooring: MERGE into 'LEE FLOORING' (all caps), preserving all products from both. Was LEE (2) beside Lee Flooring (84). Decided by Albert 2026-09-21. Note this also RENAMES the 84-product record, since it was mixed case.
_record_rulings_2026_09_21.ZION vs VIZION: DO NOT MERGE. Confirmed by Albert 2026-09-21: ZION (105 products) is a GENUINELY DIFFERENT SUPPLIER from VIZION (53). The names look like a typo split and ZION holds twice the products, so this is exactly the pair a future cleanup would merge on sight. It would be wrong.
_record_rulings_2026_09_21._capitalisation: Albert, 2026-09-21: supplier names are ALL CAPS across Notion, Airtable and Lightspeed. BRANDS ARE NOT — they keep their own case and must be preserved through any supplier merge or rename. Two LS records are still mixed case and need renaming when convenient: 'CIF Distributors' (805) and, via the merge above, 'Lee Flooring' (84).
_record_rulings_2026_09_21._still_open: Three LS names differ from Airtable by NAME, not case, so capitalising Airtable does not reach parity on its own: FAW (317) vs FLOORS AT WORK, BELLA (288) vs BELLA FLOORING PLUS, and NORTHWAY BUILDING SUPPLY (67) vs NORTHWAY. Either rename the LS record or keep the per-supplier supplier_name note in ls-upload-instructions. Undecided as of 2026-09-21.
_record_rulings_2026_09_21._other_splits_not_ruled_on: 'CIF LTD.' (36) sits beside 'CIF Distributors' (805), and 'BALTIC HOMES' (10) beside the BALTIC Notion option. Surfaced 2026-09-21, not ruled on — do not merge either without asking, given ZION/VIZION turned out to be genuinely different suppliers.

prices._verified: Confirmed 2026-09-10 against every row of the Grandeur and Lee uploads that exists in Lightspeed — 315/315 on both fields, no exceptions.
prices.price_excluding_tax: Airtable `Retail price/unit`. THIS is the retail price. 231/231 and 84/84.
prices.price_including_tax: DEPENDS ON THE ENDPOINT, and this corrects an earlier claim in this file. On the 2.0 LIST endpoint it mirrors price_excluding_tax on every product, which is why a survey of that endpoint found no 1.13x anywhere. The 3.0 FAMILY read computes it properly: ENG-VIDR-0038 reads tax_exclusive 6.79 / tax_inclusive 7.6727, which is exactly x1.13. Ontario HST is real and is applied on read; the 2.0 list simply does not compute it. Still never write it.
prices._write_rule: Set supply_price and price_excluding_tax. Never write price_including_tax.
prices._no_retail_price_field: The API has NO `retail_price` key — 0 of 14,525 products carry one. That name belongs to the CSV importer only; it maps to price_excluding_tax.
prices._tax_exclusive: Products are STORED tax-exclusive — the outlet reports display_prices 'exclusive'. The inclusive figure is derived at 13% by endpoints that compute it. A stored price that looks 13% low against a customer quote is correct.

category._differs_from_the_csv: No API value contains ' / '. The product_categories.leaves list below is the CSV-importer path form ('FLOORING / VINYL / SPC') and is NOT what the API returns or, presumably, accepts. 58 distinct leaf names exist live, well beyond the 7 the CSV path form covers — the catalogue carries PLUMBING, VANITY, HVAC, GROUT, INTERIOR DOORS and more.

variants._comment: The variant data model, established by reading the live catalogue 2026-09-10. This settles WHAT a family looks like. What a CREATE request must send to produce one is still unverified — see _create_shape_unknown.
variants._family_id: The true grouping key, and it is on EVERY product — all 14,525 carry one. A standalone product READS as a family of one. 856 families have more than one member. **This is a read-model fact and does NOT carry to the write side** — corrected 2026-09-21, after the sentence that used to end this note ('so there is no separate simple product shape to handle') sent a `variants` array on a standalone create and earned a 422. There IS a separate write shape: see create._variants_array_is_not_for_simple_products. Same class of error as supply_price — a projection in a GET response mistaken for what a POST accepts. Twice now in this one API, so treat every 'X is just a special case of Y' reading here as unproven on the write side until a write proves it.

family_structure.parent: has_variants=true, variant_parent_id=null. Exactly one per family.
family_structure._parent_is_itself_a_variant: Not an abstract container. The parent carries its own sku, own price and its own variant_options value. ENG-VIDR-0187 is the parent AND the 'Rustic' grade.
family_structure.variant_count: On the parent only. Counts the whole family INCLUDING the parent.
family_structure.button_order: Sequences the family, 1 for the parent.

variant_options._id_is_the_option_definition: Shared across every member — 02dcd191-ae89-11e8-ed44-946d1db08121 is 'Grade' throughout. Only `value` varies.
variant_options._grade_is_titans_convention: 301 products group on Grade — Character / Select / Select & Better / Rustic — which is exactly the grade-variant convention in ls-upload-instructions.

variants.variant_name: name + ' / ' + option value. Derived by Lightspeed; do not write it.

create._verified: Family shape from the API reference and the live account 2026-09-10. A STANDALONE create is now verified by a real write: LVP-FAWK-0084 -> db9e9a99-afb5-4173-8193-6ea68798d80a, 2026-09-21. A MULTI-MEMBER family create is still unverified by any write — see write_rules._variants_unverified.
create._family_is_grouped_by_name: THE critical fact. Quoting the reference: "The `name` is the field that groups a variant family. The only way products can have the same name is if they are in the same variant family." So writing a name that collides with an existing product does not merely rename it — it pulls the two into one family. This is why an update never writes `name`.
create._tax_fields: Titan is a TAX-EXCLUSIVE store, so use `outlet_taxes` (per outlet_id/tax_id). `all_outlets_tax` is for tax-inclusive stores only.

response._trap: A FLAT ARRAY OF IDS, in the order Lightspeed sorts the family by attribute value — NOT keyed by sku and not necessarily your payload order. Never map ids back to SKUs positionally. Always send an explicit `sku` per variant and re-read the family to pair them. Getting this wrong reproduces Grandeur exactly.

create._sku_is_generated_if_omitted: Lightspeed mints one from your sku sequence. Titan must ALWAYS supply its own — RULE 0 makes the Airtable SKU the source of truth.
create._variants_array_is_not_for_simple_produc: FIXED AND VERIFIED 2026-09-21. A `variants` array whose entries carry no `variant_definitions` is rejected: 422 `Each variant must have at least one variant definition`. A STANDALONE product must omit the `variants` array entirely and carry sku, prices and outlet_taxes at the TOP level — per the reference, `name` is the only required field. That matches the catalogue: 11,025 of 11,607 standalone products carry no variant options at all. Do NOT satisfy the error by inventing a one-option variant — ls-upload-instructions forbids exactly that ('a variant group with only one option is noise, not structure'). scripts/lightspeed_push.py build_family_payload() now branches: one action with no variant_option hoists to the top level, anything else keeps the array. Proven live on LVP-FAWK-0084.
create._read_back_of_a_standalone: The same asymmetry one call later, found the same day. GET /api/3.0/products/{id} on a standalone returns `variants: []` and carries the code at the TOP level (`sku_number`, and the CUSTOM entry of `product_codes`). family_by_sku() iterated `variants` alone, returned {}, and the push script read that as 'the product I just created is not there' — so a create that HAD succeeded stopped the batch and logged only a failure with a null raw_ref_action_id, which would have let a re-run create a duplicate. It now falls back to the product document itself when `variants` is empty.

update._any_member_id_works: In 2.1 any id in the family is accepted; the parent is resolved for you.
update.common: Fields shared by the whole family — name, description. Writing these hits every member.
update.details: Fields belonging to one variant — product_codes, price. Updates the id in the URL.
update._maps_onto_our_write_rule: CORRECTED 2026-09-21, the hard way. This previously said the prices-only payload catalog_reconcile.py emits maps straight onto `details`. Half true: `price_excluding_tax` does, `supply_price` does NOT. 2.1 has no such field and rejects the WHOLE request with 422 `Unknown field in payload` when it sees one. The cost is stored on the product-supplier join row, so an update writes it as `product_suppliers: [{supplier_id, price}]`. `supply_price` on the 2.0 LIST response is a convenience projection of that same number, which is exactly why the mistake stayed invisible: everything reads it, nothing can write it.
update._cannot_create: The update endpoints cannot add a variant to a family. Creates go through 2.0.
update._price_fields: Titan is tax-exclusive, so retail is `price_excluding_tax`. Never write `price_including_tax` — that is for tax-inclusive stores.
update._product_suppliers_shape: [{supplier_id, price, code?}] — no record `id`; supplier_id is the key. Sending it REPLACES that supplier row, so carry an existing `code` through or it is blanked as a side effect. Verified live 2026-09-21 on ENG-FAWK-0054: one supplier row in, one out, updated in place, no duplicate. A product with NO supplier cannot take a cost this way at all — 1,440 live products are in that state — and scripts/lightspeed_write.py stops rather than picking one.
update._multi_supplier_write: 2026-09-23 (ported from a stranded branch). A product can carry more than one supplier row, and the array REPLACES the set, so sending only the repriced row would drop the others. lightspeed_write._product_suppliers_with_price() reads the product first, sends back EVERY row, and reprices only the one whose supplier_id matches product.supplier_id. It refuses when there are no rows, or when zero or several rows match. Covered by tests/test_lightspeed.py; not yet exercised live on a multi-supplier product.
update._verified_live: 2026-09-21. 7 FAW products updated through this shape and read back: cost and retail both correct, name unchanged, supplier row count unchanged. First verified write this pipeline has ever made.

read_only_attributes._note: Read-only per the reference. They cannot be written to move a product between families or to promote a child to parent.

inheritance._comment: Children do not hold all their own data; these come from the parent.

variants._orphans_explained: The reference warns that a product not in a variant family can still carry populated variant_options — it used to be a variant and was turned back into a simple product. That is exactly the 215 products found carrying a Grade option with no parent. Never infer variant-ness from variant_options; use variant_parent_id and has_variants.

add_to_existing_family._comment: Fills the gap flagged earlier. There IS an API path for adding a variant to a family that already exists — it is a third endpoint again, and it is a POST to the 2.1 collection, not the 2.0 one used to create a family from scratch.
add_to_existing_family._joins_by_name: `common.name` is how the new variant finds its family — more confirmation that name is the family key on the API side.
add_to_existing_family._must_match_the_family_dimensions: variant_attribute_values must cover EVERY attribute the family uses. A family on Color and Size needs both.
add_to_existing_family._and_must_not_duplicate_a_combination: Two members with the same attribute values are a Duplicate Variants rejection.
add_to_existing_family._verified_live: Executed 2026-09-10, adding ENG-VIDR-0195 (Character) to the family of ENG-VIDR-0038 (Select). Three corrections to the documented shape came out of doing it.
add_to_existing_family._no_trailing_slash: The docs write it as /api/2.1/products/ with a trailing slash. That returns 404 'page not found'. Drop the slash.
add_to_existing_family._supply_price_is_not_a_field: `supply_price` is rejected with 422 'Unknown field in payload'. In 2.1 the supply price lives on product_suppliers[].price alongside supplier_id. price_excluding_tax IS accepted.

response._differs_from_2_0: The 2.0 family create returns an ARRAY of ids; this returns ONE id as a bare string. Do not assume a list.

read_family_key_names._comment: Three names for one concept across three endpoints. Reading the wrong one returns nothing, silently.
read_family_key_names.sku_on_a_3_0_variant: primary_sku_code, NOT sku. Also present as the CUSTOM entry in product_codes, which is the authoritative one.

active._note: The two always agreed: 12,934 true, 1,591 false. deleted_at was null on every product.

handles._comment: Handle format is NOT consistent across the catalogue, which matters because it is shared across a family and is what the upload CSV keys grouping on.
handles.titan_minted: Uppercase alphanumeric, supplied explicitly — GRND65EWOBORABORA, LEEFACCTMOULD. This is the format ls-upload-instructions specifies.
handles.lightspeed_generated: Lowercase slug derived from the product name when no handle is supplied — videng---7-european-white-oak-clear-tg--75-x-18mm-x-rl---3mm-top---2456sfb. The whole Vidar range is this shape.
handles._implication: Never assume a handle matches the minted format when reading. 856 handles are shared by more than one product, which is correct — that is a family.

variant_attributes._comment: Attributes must exist before a variant referencing them can be created. Titan's account already has 28. Read live: GET /api/2.0/variant_attributes.

grade.name: Grade
grade._note: Already exists and is already in use on 301 products with Character / Select / Select & Better / Rustic. Titan's grade-variant convention needs NO attribute creation.

variant_attributes._junk_present: Several attributes are clearly accidental — 'Red Oak', '31/2"*7', '5-1/4" STEP', "10'", '____ BATCH'. Note both 'Colour' and 'Color' exist. Never create an attribute automatically; pick from the live list or stop.

api_shape.categories_are_product_types: product_category and product_type are the same thing — the reference says 'Product types are now product categories', and on a live product product_type_id equals product_category.id. Resolve names via GET /api/2.0/product_types; 63 exist, flat, e.g. ENGINEERED HARDWOOD, SPC, GLUE DOWN, LOOSE LAY, ACCESSORIES.

handle_vs_name._comment: Worth stating plainly because the two entry points differ and both beliefs are half right.
handle_vs_name.csv_import: Handle is the grouping key YOU supply — rows sharing a handle become variants of one product. This is why Airtable carries LS Handle / Parent ID.
handle_vs_name.api: `name` is what Lightspeed identifies a family by. A create passes a `variants` array, so array membership does the grouping and handle is optional (Lightspeed slugs one from the name if omitted). Adding to an existing family joins it by common.name.
handle_vs_name._they_must_agree: The ls-upload-instructions skill already states the reconciliation: every row sharing a name must share one handle. In the live catalogue that holds — family members share both.
handle_vs_name._practical_rule: Read identity from variant_parent_id / has_variants, join products on sku, and treat handle as the CSV-side grouping key it is.
